subclassFeature.name: Phoenix Sorcery
entries: In a world shrouded by the encroaching shadows of the Black Dawn, true light has withered and ancient flames have grown cold. Yet beneath mountains of ash, the primordial spark of the Phoenix refuses to die. Your innate power derives from this undying flame—an eternal fire that hungers to be rekindled through destruction and miraculous rebirth. While others fear the dark, you carry within your veins the fierce, burning heart of a dying sun.

subclassFeature.name: Phoenix Magic
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Phoenix Spells table. Each spell counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.
Additionally, you learn the {@spell control flames|xge} cantrip. It counts as a sorcerer cantrip for you, but it doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

subclassFeature.name: Ignite
entries: At 1st level, you gain the ability to start fires with a touch. As a bonus action or an action, you can magically ignite an unattended flammable object you touch with your hand—such as a torch, a piece of tinder, a campfire, or the hem of drapes.

subclassFeature.name: Mantle of Flame
entries: Starting at 1st level, you can awaken the dormant ember of the phoenix burning within your soul.
As a bonus action, you magically wreathe yourself in swirling fire, soot, and incandescent embers. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

items: You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
Any creature takes fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) if it hits you with a melee attack from within 5 feet of you or if it touches you.
Once per turn, when you roll fire damage for a sorcerer spell or feature, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.
You have resistance to fire damage.

entries: You can use this feature once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. You can also expend 2 sorcery points to use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Phoenix Spark
entries: Starting at 6th level, the fiery energy within you surges outward to preserve your life in the face of defeat.

If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to draw upon the spark of the phoenix. You are instead reduced to 1 hit point, and each creature within 10 feet of you takes fire damage equal to your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier.

If you use this feature while under the effects of your Mantle of Flame, each creature instead takes fire damage equal to twice your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier, and your Mantle of Flame immediately ends.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Cinder Soul
entries: Also starting at 6th level, the eternal fire permanently fuses with your physical form and spirit. You gain permanent resistance to fire damage.
In addition, spells you cast ignore resistance to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Nourishing Fire
entries: Starting at 14th level, your destructive fire feeds and sustains your mortal frame. When you expend a spell slot or sorcery points to cast a spell of 1st level or higher that deals fire damage, you regain hit points equal to the slot's level (or sorcery points expended) + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).
Additionally, you can choose one friendly creature you can see within 30 feet of you; that creature regains hit points equal to your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Form of the Phoenix
entries: At 18th level, you master the primordial avatar of the phoenix. While your Mantle of Flame feature is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: Blazing wings of incandescent flame and dark ash sprout from your back, granting you a flying speed of 40 feet and the ability to hover.
You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and immunity to fire damage.
If you use your Phoenix Spark feature, that feature deals an extra 20 fire damage to each affected creature, and you regain hit points equal to half your hit point maximum.
